caption: Figure 111. Circular and angular object
shows: Road with reference line on top (s to the right, t up) and right lanes -1,-2,-3 below. A circular object with centre M at (s1, t1) beside lane -3, radius r. A rectangular object at (s2, t2) inside lane -3 with local u axis along s and v axis along t; 'length' is dimensioned along u, 'width' along v. t values are measured from the reference line (negative, to the right).
lesson: An object is placed by the (s, t, zOffset) of its origin, which is the centre of its bounding volume. Shape is EITHER radius (+height, cylinder) OR length+width (+height, box). In 1.9 the attribute table now agrees with the drawing: @length is along local u (road direction when hdg=0), @width along local v (lateral).
right: Write s,t,zOffset of the bounding-volume centre, not of a corner
Use length along u (s direction at hdg=0) and width along v (t direction)
Use radius only for round items (trees, poles, bollards); never combine radius with length/width
Make every point of the real object lie inside the bounding volume, and each face of the box touch the object
wrong: Swapping length and width (the 1.7 table had them reversed)
Giving both radius and width/length
Placing the origin at the object footprint edge
new_vs_1_7: Same drawing as 1.7 Figure 88, but 1.9 fixes the text inconsistency: length=u-axis, width=v-axis, height along z of the local frame. New object attributes @temporary and @invalidated (1.9).

caption: Figure 112. Placing objects on roads
shows: Side view z over s: road elevation (blue) is flat then rises in an S-shape. A long grey slab is inserted with its origin on the curve: its rear end dips below the flat road start, its front end cuts into the rising road while the middle floats above the dip.
lesson: Objects are rigid: they do not bend with elevation or superelevation. Objects placed on the road surface must be small enough that they neither cut into nor float noticeably above the road, nor cause skewed CRG surfaces.
right: Split long on-road features (painted areas, long islands) into short objects or use a repeat (which follows the road)
Use cornerRoad outlines with per-corner dz/height so the outline follows the surface
Use perpToRoad only for objects smaller than the vertical curvature radius
wrong: One long rigid object over a crest or sag
Relying on pitch/roll to fix a long object on a curved profile
new_vs_1_7: Same idea as 1.7 Figure 90; 1.9 adds the explicit warning about skewed OpenCRG surfaces and the 1.9 rule avoid_skewed_crg_surfaces tied to @perpToRoad.

caption: Figure 113. UML class diagram of the Objects class
shows: t_road_objects contains object 0..*, objectReference 0..*, tunnel 0..*, bridge 0..*. t_road_objects_object: required s (grEqZero), t, zOffset, id; optional type (e_objectType), subtype, name, dynamic (yes/no), validLength, orientation, hdg, pitch, roll, height (>=0), length (>0), width, radius (>0), perpToRoad, invalidated=false, temporary=false. Children: repeat 0..*, material 0..*, laneValidity 0..* (fromLane, toLane, layer=permanent), parkingSpace 0..1 (access, restrictions), markings 0..1 -> marking 1..* (side, weight, width, color, zOffset, spaceLength, lineLength, startOffset, stopOffset) -> cornerReference 0..* (id), borders 0..1 -> border 1..* (width, type, outlineId, useCompleteOutline), surface 0..1 -> CRG 0..1 (file, hideRoadSurfaceCRG, zScale), skeleton 0..1 -> polyline 1..* (id) -> choice vertexRoad 2..* (s,t,dz,radius,intersectionPoint,id) xor vertexLocal 2..* (u,v,z,radius,intersectionPoint,id), outlines 0..1 -> outline 1..* (id, fillType, outer=true, closed, laneType) and legacy outline 0..1; outline geometry xor: cornerRoad 2..* (s,t,dz,height,id) | curveLocal 1..* (u,v,z,height,length,hdg,id; one of line / arc(curvature) / paramPoly3(aU..dV,pRange)) | cornerLocal 2..* (u,v,z,height,id). tunnel: s,length,name,id,type,lighting,daylight. bridge: s,length,name,id,type. objectReference: s,t,id,zOffset,validLength,orientation. Constraint block lists per-type forbidden children (e.g. crosswalk: no skeleton/border/radius, repeat only distance 0; pole: no border/parking/material/marking, repeat only distance>0; tree/vegetation/building analogous) and the xor of radius vs width+length. markings constraint: markings directly under object only when no outline; marking with side cannot have cornerReference, otherwise >=2 cornerReference.
lesson: This is the authoritative data model for <objects>. Key rules for a writer: shape xor (radius | width+length), outline geometry xor (cornerRoad | cornerLocal | curveLocal), markings live under <object> only without outline and under <outline> when an outline exists, laneValidity is the same class used by signals and carries a layer.
right: Model objects as a struct with required s,t,zOffset,id and optional everything else
Emit <outlines><outline> (not the legacy single <outline>) for new files
Keep corner ids starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 when markings reference them
Respect per-type forbidden children (e.g. no <borders> except on trafficIsland)
Add @temporary/@invalidated only when true (defaults false)
wrong: Mixing cornerRoad and cornerLocal in one outline
Putting <markings> under <object> while the object also has an outline
Giving a pole/tree a continuous repeat (distance=0)
Using <borders> on non-trafficIsland objects
new_vs_1_7: Much larger than 1.7 Figure 89: adds skeleton/polyline/vertexRoad/vertexLocal (1.8), curveLocal with line/arc/paramPoly3 (1.9), outline.outer/closed/laneType, surface/CRG, laneValidity.layer (1.9), object.invalidated/temporary (1.9), repeat.detachFromReferenceLine and bT/cT/dT (1.9), and an explicit per-type constraint list.

caption: Figure 114. Traffic island as object
shows: Road with outer lanes 3 and -3 (dark red, non-driving), lanes 2 (traffic to the left) and -2 (traffic to the right). Around the reference line the boundary between lanes 2 and -2 opens into a lens; the lens is filled with orange hatched chevron area and in its middle sits a green rounded island with a dark-red pedestrian refuge strip crossing it.
lesson: A traffic island inside a road is an object (type trafficIsland) described by several outlines: one outer outline (the whole lens) and inner outlines (green body, refuge) fully inside it, each with its own fillType/laneType. The surrounding lanes widen around it rather than the island cutting the lanes.
right: Exactly one outline with outer=true; all inner outlines fully inside it
Where an inner outline touches the outer one, share the identical point
Use fillType (grass, paint, pavement...) and laneType per outline
Use cornerRoad or curveLocal for smooth island shapes
wrong: Several outer outlines on one object
Inner outline sticking out of the outer outline
Modelling the island as a lane with no width transition around it
new_vs_1_7: Same drawing as 1.7 Figure 94; 1.9 adds the rules exactly_one_outer and inner_outline_touches_outer and the explanation of multiple outlines (pedestrian refuge, curb).

caption: Figure 115. Object described by corner road coordinates
shows: Inertial X/Y grid; S-shaped road from about (10,10) to (45,55) with perpendicular s ticks every 10 m (s=0..80) and the local s/t axes at s=0. Beside it a 9-corner concave polygon with corners [s1,t1]..[s9,t9] listed counter-clockwise.
lesson: cornerRoad corners are given in road coordinates (s, t, dz, height), but in 1.9 the edges between consecutive corners are straight lines in the INERTIAL system (corners are first converted to x,y,z, then linearly interpolated). The outline does not bend between corners; to follow a curved road, add more corners.
right: Convert each corner (s,t,dz) to x,y,z first, then connect linearly
Densify corners along curved roads
List area corners counter-clockwise
Use id 0,1,2,... when markings reference corners
wrong: Interpolating the edge in s/t space (that would bend the edge with the road)
Fewer than 2 cornerRoad points
Mixing cornerRoad with cornerLocal/curveLocal in one outline
formula: e(p) = P_i + (P_{i+1} - P_i) * p, with P = (x,y,z) of corner after road->inertial transform, p in [0,1]
new_vs_1_7: The 1.7 lesson 'outline bends with the road' is replaced: 1.9 states edges are straight in inertial coordinates. New 1.9 rules: first_id_zero, sequential_id_values, mandatory id when markings exist.

caption: Figure 116. An object described by <cornerLocal> coordinates
shows: Curved road from about (15,70); s ticks 0..50. A green arrow goes from the reference line at s=20 to the object origin P (s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0, hdg=7pi/4 rad). At P a local u/v frame rotated by hdg; the same 9-corner polygon is given as [u1,v1]..[u9,v9].
lesson: cornerLocal corners are in the object's local u/v/z frame: origin = (s,t,zOffset) of the object, rotated by hdg relative to the road heading at s. The shape is rigid and independent of road curvature; ideal for buildings and islands defined from polygons.
right: Compute origin from s,t; heading = road heading(s) + hdg; transform polygon into u/v
Store z per corner relative to the origin
Use for OSM building/area polygons (convert x,y to u,v around a chosen centroid)
wrong: Treating hdg as an inertial heading (it is relative to the road)
Using cornerLocal for long features that must follow the road
formula: x = x0 + u*cos(H) - v*sin(H), y = y0 + u*sin(H) + v*cos(H), H = roadHdg(s) + hdg
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 96; 1.9 adds id rules and the exclusivity rule including curveLocal.

caption: Figure 117. An object described by <cornerLocal> coordinates using <paramPoly3> elements
shows: Same road and origin P (s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0, hdg=7pi/4) as Figure 116, but the outline is a smooth blob: straight segments [u1,v1]->[u2,v2]->[u3,v3]->[u4,v4], then a large smooth curve from [u4,v4] round to [u5,v5] and a concave curve to [u6,v6] before a straight edge back.
lesson: New 1.9 curveLocal: each outline vertex starts a curve (line, arc with constant curvature, or paramPoly3 in u/v) with @hdg and optional @length; the curve must end exactly at the next vertex (continuity). This gives smooth traffic islands and painted shapes without dense polygons.
right: Use curveLocal with arc for round island noses, paramPoly3 for measured shapes
Ensure each curve ends at the next vertex (continuous_curve_local)
Set pRange (arcLength or normalized) consistently with coefficients
Make @length match the integrated curve length
wrong: Mixing curveLocal with cornerLocal/cornerRoad in one outline
Leaving gaps between successive curves
Using normalized coefficients with p up to length
formula: u(p)=aU+bU p+cU p^2+dU p^3, v(p)=aV+bV p+cV p^2+dV p^3; arc: constant curvature (positive = left/CCW)
new_vs_1_7: Entirely new in 1.9 (no 1.7 counterpart). Caption wording says cornerLocal but the section is curveLocal.

caption: Figure 118. Example of the bounding volume and skeleton of a traffic light pole
shows: Perspective road (s up the image, t to the left). A traffic-light pole object at @s=25, @t=1.5 with bounding box width=3 (along t), length=0.3 (along s), height=4. Inside the box: polyline id=1 is the vertical pole whose bottom vertex is marked 'intersection point' (touches ground); polyline id=2 is the arm, kinking from the pole and running horizontally across over the road.
lesson: Skeleton (1.8+) refines a bounding box with polylines of vertices that each carry radius (or width/length) giving cylinders/frustums. One vertex can be flagged intersectionPoint=true where the object meets the ground. Mast arms are separate polylines.
right: Model mast-arm traffic light poles as pole/trafficLight with a skeleton: polyline for mast (first vertex intersectionPoint) and polyline for arm
Keep all vertices and their radius boundaries inside the bounding box
Use the same parameter style (radius OR width+length) for all vertices of one polyline
wrong: Bounding box that does not cover the arm
Mixing vertexRoad and vertexLocal in one polyline
Using radius and width/length on the same vertex
new_vs_1_7: New since 1.8 (skeleton absent in 1.7). Also illustrates that width is along t and length along s for objects.

caption: Figure 119. Example of the skeleton of a tree
shows: Road on the left (s up, t left). A tree at @s=9, @t=-5, @zOffset=-1 to the right of the road. Large grey bounding box; inside, polyline id=1 is the thin trunk (cylinder) whose lower vertex is the intersection point with the ground (zOffset below road level), polyline id=2 is the crown drawn as a wide cylinder on top.
lesson: A tree can be described by two vertexLocal polylines (trunk and crown) with radius per vertex, letting a simulator know vehicles can pass under the crown. zOffset can be negative when the terrain is below the road reference.
right: Use type=tree with radius bounding cylinder or box, plus optional skeleton trunk+crown
Mark the ground contact vertex with intersectionPoint=true
wrong: Single opaque bounding box only, when clearance under the crown matters
Vertices outside the bounding box
new_vs_1_7: New since 1.8. Replaces the 1.7 suggestion of two outlines for trunk/crown with the more natural skeleton (outlines also remain possible).

caption: Figure 120. Large angular continuous object with changing shape using a single <repeat> element
shows: Top view: curved two-lane road (lanes -1, -2). A blue continuous band starts at s (tStart, widthStart) and runs 'length' along the reference line to tEnd/widthEnd, following the curve and narrowing; its centre dash-dot line moves closer to the road. Side view: band height shrinks from heightStart to heightEnd while zOffset rises from zOffsetStart to zOffsetEnd.
lesson: repeat with distance=0 extrudes the object profile into one continuous feature (guard rail, wall). t, width, height, zOffset are interpolated from *Start to *End over the length; lengthStart/End are ignored for continuous objects. By default it follows the reference line curvature.
right: Use distance=0 for guard rails, walls, fences, hedges
Set tStart/tEnd, widthStart/End, heightStart/End, zOffsetStart/End
Set detachFromReferenceLine=true only for a straight segment that should not follow the road
wrong: Continuous repeat for objects with outline or skeleton changing dimensions
Using widthStart/End on a radius-defined object
new_vs_1_7: Same picture as 1.7 Figure 91; 1.9 adds detachFromReferenceLine semantics and cubic t (bT,cT,dT).

caption: Figure 121. Repeated small angular objects with changing shape using a single <repeat> element
shows: Top view: discrete blue rectangles every 'distance' starting at s, each rotated to the local road heading; centres follow a dash-dot line from tStart to tEnd; size shrinks from widthStart/lengthStart to widthEnd/lengthEnd. Side view: heights shrink, zOffset rises. The final position at s+length has no instance because length/distance is not an integer.
lesson: repeat with distance>0 places floor(length/distance)+... instances: only instances whose origin lies inside [s, s+length] are created; no partial instance; instance extents may overhang the section and are not clipped.
right: Instance origins at s + k*distance while <= s+length
Rotate each instance with road heading
Interpolate dimensions linearly unless polynomial t given
wrong: Adding a final instance at s+length when length is not a multiple of distance
Clipping instance geometry at section ends
formula: count = floor(length/distance) + 1 (origins at ds = 0, distance, 2*distance, ... <= length)
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 92 but 1.9 text explicitly states the rounding-down rule and no-clipping rule.

caption: Figure 122. Repeated small circular objects with changing shape using a single <repeat> element
shows: Same layout with circles shrinking from radiusStart to radiusEnd, centres along tStart->tEnd; side view heights shrink and zOffset grows to zOffsetEnd.
lesson: Circular objects repeat with radiusStart/radiusEnd; width/length overrides are not applicable when radius is set.
right: Use radiusStart/End for poles, bollards, trees in a row
distance>0 for discrete posts/lamps
wrong: widthStart/widthEnd on radius objects (rule no_widthstart_end_with_radius)
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 93; new 1.9 rule forbids width interpolation on radius objects.

caption: Figure 123. Parking spaces rectangular (left figure) and rhomboid (right figure)
shows: Left: road with reference line on top, lanes -1, -2, and a parking strip below; three axis-aligned orange rectangles with origins (s1,t1),(s2,t2),(s3,t3). Right: same, but the rectangles are rotated about their origins (angled bays, rotation arrow shown).
lesson: Each bay is one object of type parkingSpace placed by s/t; angled bays use hdg (rotation around the origin). Access restrictions go in the <parkingSpace access restrictions> child.
right: One parkingSpace object per bay with width/length bounding box
Use hdg for angled parking
Use object markings with side for bay lines when there is no outline
Parking bays are on a parking lane (lane type parking) or in a lot
wrong: One large object for a whole row of bays without repeat
Using radius for parking spaces (not allowed)
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 97; 1.9 type table says width/length bounding box mandatory, outline optional, repeat with distance>0 optional.

caption: Figure 124. Crosswalk in ASAM OpenDRIVE
shows: Two-lane road: lane 1 above and lane -1 below the reference line, each 3.50 m wide. A trapezoid crosswalk area: top corners at s1=5.00 and s4=15.00 (outer edge of lane 1), bottom corners at s2=8.00 and s3=12.00 (outer edge of lane -1). The two slanted sides carry dashed white/grey edge markings.
lesson: A crosswalk is an object (type crosswalk) with a cornerRoad outline spanning both lanes; its edge lines are <marking> elements placed INSIDE the <outline> and referencing corner ids (cornerReference). Crosswalk objects alone are not used for pedestrian simulation; pedestrian paths should be crossPaths in a junction.
right: Outline corners with ids 0..3 in road coordinates
markings inside the outline referencing two corner ids each
orientation=none for both directions
Also model a crossPath/junction if pedestrians must be simulated
wrong: markings directly under <object> while an outline exists (1.9 rule markings_with_outline)
Referencing non-consecutive corners without listing the points in between
new_vs_1_7: Same drawing as 1.7 Figure 98, but 1.9 moves markings inside <outline> when outlines exist (1.7 placed them under the object), and the type table recommends crossPath in junctions for pedestrian simulation.

caption: Figure 125. Tunnel
shows: Top view: road with lanes 3,2,1 (traffic to the left) and -1,-2 (traffic to the right); a grey box labelled tunnel covers the full width over an s range. Side view below: a truck and car on a road passing under a green earth mound.
lesson: A tunnel is a <tunnel s length type> under <objects>, valid for the whole cross-section unless restricted by laneValidity; the road carrying it is the part that is in the tunnel/underpass.
right: Emit <tunnel> on the road that runs inside (OSM tunnel=yes / layer<0)
Use type standard/underpass, lighting/daylight 0..1 if known
wrong: Modelling tunnels as generic <object>
Putting the tunnel on the road above
new_vs_1_7: Same concept as 1.7 Figure 99; 1.9 drawing adds a side view.

caption: Figure 126. Bridge
shows: Top view: same road with a grey box labelled bridge covering the full width over a shorter s range. Side view: bus and car on a road deck carried over an opening by abutments.
lesson: A bridge is a <bridge s length type> on the road that leads over the bridge, valid for the whole cross-section unless restricted.
right: Emit <bridge> on the road on top (OSM bridge=yes)
type concrete/steel/brick/wood
wrong: Putting the bridge on the road passing underneath
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 100 with a side view added.

caption: Figure 127. CRG for objects
shows: Curved reference line s. A green t vector from the line to the centre of a rotated chequered CRG patch; CRG axes u (along object heading) and v drawn at the patch centre labelled (0|0)CRG.
lesson: Object CRG uses the object's local u/v frame with origin at the object centre (u/v positive and negative); the CRG file's own reference line, heading and position are ignored; the patch rotates with the object.
right: Only angular (box) objects may carry surface CRG
Reference the object on every road it overlaps (objectReference)
Bounding volumes of CRG objects must not overlap
wrong: CRG on circular objects or objects with outlines
More than one CRG file per object
Continuous repeat of CRG objects
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 101; 1.9 adds rule avoid_skewed_crg_surfaces and says @height/@zOffset are ignored for surface elevation.

caption: (no caption) road surface CRG mode=attached, hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true
shows: Side view z over s: road elevation (blue) flat then rising; a stepped road-surface CRG profile rides on it between sStart and sEnd; inside the object extent the steps are replaced by one smooth flat-topped block following the OpenDRIVE elevation.
lesson: With an attached road CRG and hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true the object CRG replaces the road CRG: height = OpenDRIVE + object CRG.
right: Default hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true is only valid for attached road CRG or no road CRG
wrong: Ignoring the mode of the underlying road CRG
new_vs_1_7: In 1.7 this was img101; 1.9 file numbering differs (object_14 = attached/hide=true).

caption: (no caption) road surface CRG mode=attached, hideRoadSurfaceCRG=false
shows: Same profile; inside the object extent the object's fine bumps (darker bars) are stacked on top of the stepped road-surface CRG.
lesson: attached + hide=false: height = OpenDRIVE + road CRG + object CRG.
right: Set hideRoadSurfaceCRG=false when the object adds detail on top of road texture
new_vs_1_7: Corresponds to 1.7 img102.

caption: (no caption) road surface CRG mode attached0 / genuine / global, hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true (not allowed)
shows: Road elevation rises but the road CRG data stays near z=0 (absolute data); inside the object range a flat block sits on the CRG data, ignoring the elevation curve.
lesson: For attached0/genuine/global road CRG the combination hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true is NOT allowed.
right: Force hideRoadSurfaceCRG=false when the road CRG mode is not attached
wrong: hide=true over attached0/genuine/global road CRG
new_vs_1_7: Corresponds to 1.7 img103.

caption: (no caption) road surface CRG mode attached0 / genuine / global, hideRoadSurfaceCRG=false
shows: Same absolute road CRG near z=0; the object bumps are added on top of the road CRG profile inside the object range.
lesson: Absolute road CRG + hide=false: height = road CRG + object CRG (OpenDRIVE elevation not added).
new_vs_1_7: Corresponds to 1.7 img104.

caption: (no caption) no road surface CRG, hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true and =false
shows: Only the OpenDRIVE elevation curve with the object block sitting on it between sStart and sEnd; the same image is used for both hide values.
lesson: Without road CRG the flag has no effect: height = OpenDRIVE + object CRG. Where crgEvaluv2z returns NaN the object contributes nothing (allows non-rectangular manholes).
right: Return NaN-as-no-object when sampling outside CRG data
new_vs_1_7: Corresponds to 1.7 img105/img106 (1.9 reuses one file for both cells).

caption: Figure 128. Signals in ASAM OpenDRIVE
shows: Perspective road (s along the reference line, t to the left) with three items highlighted as signals: a painted zebra crossing, a 60 speed-limit sign at the right roadside and a traffic light at the right roadside. A faded painted turn arrow on the left lane is NOT highlighted.
lesson: Signals are traffic signs, traffic lights AND binding road markings that regulate traffic (zebra, painted speed). Non-binding markings such as plain arrows are objects (roadMark) or lane road marks.
right: Emit traffic lights and regulatory signs as <signal>
Binding painted markings may be signals; guidance arrows are roadMark objects
Place signals relative to the road they govern (s,t)
wrong: Emitting painted turn arrows as signals
Emitting traffic lights as objects
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 102 plus the explicit faded arrow (non-signal).

caption: Figure 129. Width and height for signal
shows: XML of a German 100 km/h sign (s=3981.4158159146, t=-14.0503, id=5000162, name Vorschriftzeichen, dynamic=no, orientation=+, zOffset=3.8835, country=DE, countryRevision=2017, type=274, subtype=100, value=100, unit=km/h, height=0.77, width=0.77, hOffset=5.7595865) beside the round sign with width and height 0.77 m dimensioned on the plate.
lesson: width/height describe the sign plate only (not the post); zOffset is to the plate bottom. type/subtype are unique only with country+countryRevision; value requires unit. In 1.9 width is along local v and an optional @length gives plate thickness along u.
right: Always pair value with unit
Set country (ISO 3166 alpha-2) and countryRevision
Use country='OpenDRIVE' with the ASAM signal catalogue for items without official codes (traffic lights)
wrong: value without unit
height including the post
type/subtype without country
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 103. New: @length thickness, @invalidated, @temporary (1.9), and the OpenDRIVE signal catalogue for generic traffic lights.

caption: Figure 130. Orientation and hOffset for signal
shows: Left: right-hand-traffic perspective road with reference line pointing away. Middle: 100 sign on a post, @zOffset dimensioned from road level to the bottom of the plate, @orientation='+'. Right: top view, reference line pointing up, sign at the right roadside; dashed line back to the reference line; red line = plate rotated by @hOffset measured counter-clockwise from the negative reference-line direction.
lesson: orientation '+' = applies to traffic moving in +s; with hOffset=0 the face points toward -s (toward approaching drivers). hOffset is a CCW rotation from that base; for '-' the base is +s. For orientation=none hOffset is relative to the reference line.
right: Default hOffset=0 for normal signs facing approaching traffic
For RHT +s traffic place sign at negative t (right side) with orientation '+'
Compute face heading = roadHdg(s) + pi + hOffset for '+', roadHdg(s) + hOffset for '-'
wrong: Setting hOffset=pi to 'face traffic' (double rotation)
orientation '+' on a sign for -s traffic
formula: faceHeading('+') = hdg_ref(s) + pi + hOffset; faceHeading('-') = hdg_ref(s) + hOffset
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 104; 1.9 text adds the hOffset meaning for orientation=none.

caption: Figure 131. UML class diagram of the Signals class
shows: t_road_signals has signal 0..* (class t_road_signals_signal_road) and signalReference 0..* (s,t,id,orientation, with validity 0..*). Abstract t_road_signals_signal: id, name[0..1], dynamic, orientation, country[0..1], countryRevision[0..1], type, subtype, value[0..1], text[0..1], unit[0..1], height[0..1], length[0..1], hOffset[0..1], width[0..1], roll[0..1], pitch[0..1], invalidated=false, temporary=false; children validity 0..* (laneValidity fromLane,toLane,layer), dependency 0..* (id, type[0..1]), reference 0..* (elementType object|signal, elementId, type[0..1]), semantics 0..1, physicalPosition 0..1 (xor positionRoad | positionInertial, both marked deprecated). t_road_signals_signal_road specialises it with s, t, zOffset and constraint: type multiBoard => dynamic=true and >=1 vmsBoard and >=1 staticBoard. t_road_signals_board_sign specialises signal with v, z. Abstract t_road_signals_board with subclasses staticBoard (sign 0..*) and vmsBoard (displayType, displayHeight, displayWidth, v, z; displayArea 0..* index,width,height,v,z); signal_road has staticBoard 0..* and vmsBoard 0..*.
lesson: Signals are road-anchored (s,t,zOffset). Each signal can carry lane validity, dependencies (supplementary plates), references to objects/signals (e.g. stop line), semantics, and boards. Physical position is deprecated: place the signal where it physically stands.
right: Required on signal: id, s, t, zOffset, orientation, dynamic, type, subtype
Use <reference elementType='object' elementId=stopLineId> from a traffic light to its stop line
Use <semantics> for behaviour (speed, priority, prohibited...)
Use staticBoard/vmsBoard children for sign assemblies
wrong: Emitting <positionRoad>/<positionInertial> in new 1.9 output
Using <dependency> to link a traffic light to its stop line (dependency is for supplementary signs)
new_vs_1_7: Expanded from 1.7 Figure 105: adds length, invalidated, temporary, semantics, boards (staticBoard/vmsBoard/displayArea/board_sign), the signal/signal_road split, laneValidity.layer, and marks physicalPosition deprecated.

caption: Figure 132. Lanes with signals in the shape of road markings
shows: Road with lanes 4,3,2,1 (traffic to the left, gray arrows) and -1,-2 (traffic to the right). Painted speed numbers: 60 in lane 3, 80 in lane 2, 100 in lane 1 (all readable for leftward traffic) and 80 in lane -1 (readable for rightward traffic); each is a separate signal.

caption: Figure 148. Touching Points between 2 logically connected roads
shows: Four panels of road 1 (angled two-lane) linked to road 2 (horizontal), red dots = touching points at lane edges. Panel 1 (X): a visible gap between the roads. Panel 2 (X): roads overlap with the edges laterally shifted, touching points do not coincide. Panel 3 (X): centre points coincide but road 1 meets road 2 at an angle (kink). Panel 4 (check): curved road 1 flows into curved road 2; all three touching points coincide and headings match.
lesson: Logically linked drivable lanes must meet with matching x,y (no horizontal gap), matching heading (no kink), matching z and roll (no vertical gap) and should match pitch (no vertical kink), within floating tolerance.
right: Check every predecessor/successor link: position, heading, z, roll, pitch at lane-edge touching points
Account for reference line direction (contactPoint start/end) when comparing headings
Fix geometry, not just links
wrong: Linking roads whose ends are separated or overlap
Linking roads that meet at an angle

caption: Figure 149. Touching Points within laneSections

Ensure lane links between sections pair lanes whose edges coincide
Keep laneOffset continuous (value and slope)
wrong: Width jumps at section boundaries
laneOffset with discontinuous value or derivative

caption: Figure 150. Touching Points for connecting roads
shows: Incoming road with lanes -1,-2 enters a dashed junction area; two connecting roads (lane -1 each) leave: one curves up-right into an outgoing road, one straight. Touching points at start and end of each connecting road coincide with incoming/outgoing lane edges. Marked correct.
lesson: Connecting roads must start exactly at the incoming lane edges and end exactly at the outgoing lane edges with matching heading.
right: Fit connecting road geometry to the touching points and headings of both ends
Validate every connection's both ends
wrong: Connecting road starting at the reference line of the incoming road when its lane is offset

caption: Figure 151. Touching Points for multiple lane linkage
shows: Aerial road photo: lane -1 splits into lanes -1 (left-turn arrow) and -2 (right-turn arrow). Red touching points on the outer edges; a yellow point at the start of the new dividing line labelled 'Not a Touching Point' because lane -1 has two successors.

wrong: Flagging a smoothness error at the inner split point

figure: UML Core (ch. 6.3 root element / ch. 7 additional data)
caption: UML class diagram 'Core' (OpenDRIVE root and g_additionalData)
shows: OpenDRIVE::t_OpenDRIVE contains header (1), road 1..*, vmsGroup 0..*, controller 0..*, junction 0..*, junctionGroup 0..*, station 0..*; all classes specialise _OpenDriveElement which carries g_additionalData 0..*: userData 0..* (code, value[0..1], any content), include 0..* (file), dataQuality 0..1 (error 0..1: xyAbsolute, zAbsolute, xyRelative, zRelative; rawData 0..1: date, source, sourceComment[0..1], postProcessing, postProcessingComment[0..1]). Simple types t_zeroOne, t_grEqZero, t_grZero (double) and union t_grEqZeroOrContactPoint.
lesson: Element order under <OpenDRIVE>: header, road+, then vmsGroup/controller/junction/junctionGroup/station. Every element may carry userData/include/dataQuality. At least one road is required.
right: Write header first, then roads, then controllers, junctions, junctionGroups, stations
Use dataQuality rawData source='sensor'/'custom' + postProcessing for OSM-derived data
Put OSM ids in userData (code='osm_id')
wrong: File with zero roads
Custom attributes instead of userData
new_vs_1_7: 1.9 adds vmsGroup at top level (1.8) and t_grEqZeroOrContactPoint union for junction boundaries.

caption: UML class diagram 'Header'
shows: t_header: revMajor, revMinor (integer), name, version, date, north, south, east, west, vendor (all [0..1]); children geoReference 0..1, offset 0..1 (x,y,z,hdg), license 0..1 (name, spdxid[0..1], text[0..1], resource[0..1]), defaultRegulations 0..1 -> roadRegulations 0..* (type e_roadType) and signalRegulations 0..* (type, subtype), each with semantics 0..1.
lesson: Header can now declare a license (useful for ODbL OSM data) and default regulations per road type with semantics (e.g. default urban speed).
right: revMajor=1, revMinor=9
Add <license name='ODbL-1.0' spdxid='ODbL-1.0'> for OSM-derived maps
Use defaultRegulations to state default speed per road type instead of placing signs everywhere
wrong: Omitting geoReference when coordinates are projected
new_vs_1_7: license and defaultRegulations are new since 1.8.

caption: UML class diagram 'Road'
shows: t_road: name[0..1], length (grZero), id {id}, junction (string), rule e_trafficRule[0..1]; children link 0..1, type 0..* (s, type e_roadType, country[0..1]) -> speed 0..1 (max t_maxSpeed = number or string, unit), planView 1, elevationProfile 0..1, lateralProfile 0..1, lanes 1..2, objects 0..1, signals 0..1, surface 0..1, railroad 0..1. e_countryCode accepts ISO alpha-2 (alpha-3 deprecated).
lesson: Road has exactly one planView and one or two <lanes> (second for a lane layer), optional objects/signals/railroad. rule sets RHT/LHT per road.
right: Write @rule='RHT' (or LHT) explicitly
junction='-1' for non-junction roads
Use 2-letter country codes
wrong: Two <lanes> without distinct layers
Alpha-3 country codes
new_vs_1_7: lanes multiplicity 1..2 (lane layers) and rule attribute are newer than 1.7's single lanes.

caption: UML class diagram 'RoadGeometry'
shows: planView -> geometry 1..* (s, x, y, hdg, length>0) with one of line, spiral (curvStart, curvEnd), arc (curvature), poly3 (deprecated; a,b,c,d), paramPoly3 (aU..dV, pRange). elevationProfile -> elevation 0..* (s,a,b,c,d). lateralProfile with constraint crossSectionSurface xor (superelevation/shape): superelevation 0..* (s,a,b,c,d), shape 0..* (s,t,a,b,c,d), crossSectionSurface 0..1 -> tOffset 0..1, surfaceStrips 1 -> strip 1..4 (id, mode) each with width/constant/linear/quadratic/cubic 0..1 -> coefficients 1..* (s,a,b,c,d). surface -> CRG 0..* (file, sStart, sEnd, orientation, mode, purpose, sOffset, tOffset, xOffset, yOffset, zOffset, zScale, hOffset).
lesson: Plan view primitives for writing; poly3 is deprecated (use paramPoly3). crossSectionSurface cannot be combined with superelevation or shape.
right: Emit line/arc/spiral/paramPoly3 only
Do not mix crossSectionSurface with superelevation/shape
wrong: Writing poly3 geometry in new files
new_vs_1_7: crossSectionSurface (1.8) and CRG x/yOffset (1.9) are new; poly3 deprecated.

caption: UML class diagram 'Link'
shows: t_road_link -> predecessor 0..1, successor 0..1 of t_road_link_predecessorSuccessor: elementId, elementType (road|junction), contactPoint[0..1], elementS[0..1], elementDir[0..1].
lesson: Road links point to a road (with contactPoint) or a junction; elementS/elementDir allow linking into the middle of a road (virtual junction context).
right: contactPoint mandatory when elementType=road
Omit contactPoint for junction links
wrong: contactPoint on a junction link
new_vs_1_7: Unchanged in essence; elementS/elementDir exist since 1.6.

caption: UML class diagram 'Lanes'
shows: t_road_lanes: layer [0..1]=permanent; constraints: permanent layer laneSections have no @length; if laneOffset exists no lane may use border. laneOffset 0..* (s,a,b,c,d); laneSection 1..* (s, length[0..1], singleSide[0..1]) -> center 1 (lane 1, id=0, type/level deprecated), left 0..1 (lane 1..*, id positive), right 0..1 (lane 1..*, id negative). Lane (t_road_lanes_laneSection_lr_lane): type, advisory=none, direction=standard, dynamicLaneType, dynamicLaneDirection, level, roadWorks=false; link 0..1 -> predecessor/successor 0..* (id, layer=permanent); choice width 1..* xor border 1..*; roadMark 0..*; height 0..* (sOffset, inner, outer); rule 0..* (sOffset, value); material 0..*; speed 0..* (sOffset, max, unit); access 0..* (sOffset, rule allow/deny, restriction deprecated) -> restriction 0..* (type).
lesson: Lane model for writing: width polynomials (not border when laneOffset present), multiple predecessors/successors allowed (lane splits), lane access with nested restriction children, direction/advisory attributes, center lane type deprecated.
right: Use width (not border)
Write access as <access sOffset rule='allow'><restriction type='bus'/></access>
Allow multiple successor ids at lane splits
wrong: border lanes together with laneOffset
Using deprecated access@restriction attribute
Setting type on the center lane
new_vs_1_7: advisory, direction, dynamicLane*, roadWorks, link layer, nested access restriction are post-1.7 additions.

caption: UML class diagram 'RoadMark'
shows: t_road_lanes_laneSection_lcr_lane_roadMark: sOffset, type, weight[0..1], color, material[0..1], width[0..1], laneChange[0..1], height[0..1]; sway 0..* (ds,a,b,c,d), type 0..1 (name, width) -> line 1..* (length, space, tOffset, sOffset, rule, width, color), explicit 0..1 -> line 1..* (length, tOffset, sOffset, rule, width).
lesson: Lane boundary markings; complex patterns via type/line; explicit lines for surveyed dashes.
right: color is required
Use laneChange to express crossing permission
wrong: Using lane roadMarks for stop lines or crosswalks (those are objects/signals)
new_vs_1_7: Unchanged structure vs 1.7 apart from minor attribute types.

caption: UML class diagram 'Junction'
shows: Abstract t_junction (name[0..1], id) with planView 0..1 (junction reference line), surface 0..1, elevationGrid 0..1, boundary 0..1, objects 0..1, controller 0..* (id, type, sequence), priority 0..* (high, low), crossPath 0..* (crossingRoad, id, roadAtStart, roadAtEnd; startLaneLink/endLaneLink 1 each: s, from, to). Subclasses: t_junction_common (type default; connection 0..* of t_junction_connection_common: connectingRoad), t_junction_direct (connection 1..* with linkedRoad), t_junction_virtual (mainRoad, sStart, sEnd, orientation; connection_virtual (deprecated, with predecessor/successor) xor connection_virtual_default), t_junction_crossing (roadSection 1..*: id, roadId, sStart, sEnd). Base t_junction_connection: id, incomingRoad[0..1], contactPoint[0..1]; laneLink 0..* (from, to, overlapZone[0..1], fromLayer, toLayer).
lesson: Junctions can carry their own <objects> (e.g. crosswalks attached to the junction reference line) and controllers; pedestrian crossings are crossPaths; crossing junction type models road/rail crossings.
right: Attach junction-wide objects (crosswalks, stop lines spanning several connecting roads) to the junction <objects> with a junction planView
Reference controllers from the junction
Use crossPath for pedestrian crossings inside junctions
wrong: Using deprecated virtual connection predecessor/successor
new_vs_1_7: Junction-level planView/objects/boundary/elevationGrid/crossPath and crossing type are new since 1.8.

caption: UML class diagram 'JunctionBoundary'
shows: t_junction_boundary -> segment 1..* (abstract, roadId) specialised as segment_lane (type lane, boundaryLane, sStart, sEnd as grEqZero or contactPoint) and segment_joint (type joint, contactPoint, jointLaneStart[0..1], jointLaneEnd[0..1], transitionLength[0..1]).
lesson: The junction area outline is built from lane segments along connecting roads and joint segments across road ends.
right: Alternate lane and joint segments to close the boundary
new_vs_1_7: New since 1.8.

caption: UML class diagram 'ElevationGrid'
shows: t_junction_elevationGrid (sStart, gridSpacing) -> elevation 0..* (left[0..1], center, right[0..1] as space-separated double lists t_junction_grid_position_list).
lesson: Junction surface height sampled on a grid along the junction reference line.
right: Use gridSpacing consistent with junction planView length
new_vs_1_7: New since 1.8.

caption: UML class diagram 'JunctionGroup'
shows: t_junctionGroup (name[0..1], id, type e_junctionGroup_type) -> junctionReference 1..* (junction).
lesson: Groups junctions (e.g. roundabout) at top level.
right: At least one junctionReference
new_vs_1_7: Same as 1.7 Figure 85.
